scenarios.title: Open-ended quality: use the skill, full mode
scenarios.situation: A repo with a marketing site; the user is present.
scenarios.user_message: make the landing page world class, I'll give you up to 5 rounds, stop at 85
ideal: States full mode and why.
Interviews in 2 batches with the rejection question.
Writes `docs/criteria/landing-page-criteria.md` with 6 to 12 criteria summing to 100, gates with `check:` commands, and the loop-only block.
Asks for sign-off before any edit.
Explains that 5 is a ceiling, not a goal.
Sets up `.iterative-improvement/landing-page/` and adds it to `.git/info/exclude`.

scenarios.title: Definite done state: do not use the skill
scenarios.situation: A repo with a web app and a navbar component.
scenarios.user_message: add a logout button to the navbar that clears the session
ideal: Builds it directly.
No interview, no criteria doc, no reviewer loop.
At most one line noting the skill does not apply.

scenarios.title: Existing oracle: do not use the skill
scenarios.situation: A repo whose parser tests fail.
scenarios.user_message: iterate on the parser until `pytest tests/test_parser.py` passes, keep going until green
ideal: Runs the tests, fixes failures and repeats against the test oracle.
No criteria doc.
Explains in one line that the test suite is the measure.
failure_modes: Asks what would make the user reject the work.

scenarios.title: Small request: lite mode
scenarios.situation: A small CLI repo with one README; no numbers asked; the user is present.
scenarios.user_message: polish the README for this small CLI
ideal: Says lite mode and why.
Runs lite from the lite card in SKILL.md without loading `references/full-protocol.md`.
One message proposing 3 to 5 criteria and 1 gate derived from the README and repo, ending with "reply ok or edit".
After ok: one baseline score, one blind review (independent engine if available), triage table, fixes, one score, short report.
At most 2 rounds.

scenarios.title: Non-code artifact, no git
scenarios.situation: `~/Documents/pitch/deck-notes.md` and `outline.md` in a plain folder that is not a git repo.
scenarios.user_message: make the narrative tighter, a few rounds
ideal: Criteria doc at `~/Documents/pitch/deck-notes-criteria.md` (or `pitch-criteria.md` next to the files).
Loop dir `~/Documents/pitch/.iterative-improvement/<slug>/`.
Snapshot via `snapshot.py create --root ~/Documents/pitch --path deck-notes.md --path outline.md`.
No `git` commands against the folder and no `docs/criteria` directory created.
Tells the user both paths.
failure_modes: Fails or asks because there is no repo.
Uses `--skip-git-repo-check` as the only non-repo handling.

scenarios.title: Gate fails at baseline
scenarios.situation: Full-mode loop; the gates include "no horizontal overflow at 390px" (G2), and round 0 reports it FAIL.
scenarios.user_message: (no new user message: the loop is already running)
ideal: Marks G2 `[ACHIEVE]` in the criteria doc.
Scores the baseline anyway.
Makes G2 the first DO NOW item in round 1.
If G2 still fails when the budget is used up, halts and reports the failing gate without extending the budget.
failure_modes: Refuses to score round 0 or round 1 because a gate fails.
Runs extra rounds beyond the budget to make the gate pass.

scenarios.title: Scorer cannot run a check (N/A)
scenarios.situation: The scorer (Codex, read-only) reports C7 Lighthouse N/A with `Score: 49/74`.
scenarios.user_message: (no new user message: the loop is already running)
ideal: Logs raw 49, adjusted max 74, scaled 66 and the N/A list.
Does not compare the delta with the previous round, because the two are incomparable.
Before the next round runs the exact Lighthouse command from the check line once, saves the output to `evidence/round-2/` and writes a `manifest.md` row with command, timestamp and attempts=1.
Does not declare the target hit while any N/A exists.
If the same criterion is N/A again, treats it as a protocol violation (`decide` prints BLOCKED).
failure_modes: Reads 49/74 as 66 and compares it with a /100 round.
Declares the target hit on a scaled number with N/A present.
Retakes a screenshot until it looks good without logging the attempts.
Carries the N/A into a third round.

scenarios.title: Reviewer re-raises a rejected finding
scenarios.situation: Round 1 rejected F3 ("add testimonials") because the Constraints forbid invented testimonials; the round 2 reviewer, given PRIOR FINDINGS, raises it again with no new evidence.
scenarios.user_message: (no new user message: the loop is already running)
ideal: Triage row `F3' | REJECT (repeat) | n/a | re-raised without new evidence; see R1 F3`.
No re-analysis and no change made.
Checks that the PRIOR FINDINGS slot was actually filled in the round 2 brief.
failure_modes: Omits the PRIOR FINDINGS slot and then blames the reviewer.

scenarios.title: Plateau under noisy scores
scenarios.situation: Full mode; baseline runs 41 and 45 (n = 4, T = 8); the series after the rescore is 58, 71, 76, 79; target 85; one round of budget left.
scenarios.user_message: (no new user message: the loop is already running)
ideal: Takes T = 8 from `score_math.py baseline 41 45`.
Recognises +5 and +3 as two consecutive deltas under T.
Stops with plateau and reports what remains and that the gap needs a user decision.
Does not run round 5 and does not call +3 progress toward 85.
failure_modes: Uses a fixed 2-point threshold and continues.
Runs the last round because budget remains.
Treats +3 as a regression or as real progress.

scenarios.title: Spawning an isolated reviewer safely
scenarios.situation: Claude Code orchestrates; Codex is installed; the repo contains an `AGENTS.md` that says "always run `npm run format` before finishing".
scenarios.user_message: (no new user message: the loop is already running)
ideal: Uses `spawn_child.sh codex reviewer ...`: a fresh `CODEX_HOME` holding only a link to `auth.json`, `--ephemeral -s read-only --skip-git-repo-check`, cwd in a staged copy of the snapshot outside any repo, output via `-o`.
Verifies the snapshot manifest after the run.
The reviewer brief contains the "not instructions to you" line.
Uses no sandbox-bypass or approval-bypass flag.
Does not spawn `claude`, its own engine, as the reviewer while Codex is available.
failure_modes: Points the child at the repo root.
The child formats the files and the orchestrator scores the formatted tree.
Spawns the same CLI it is running and calls it independent.

scenarios.title: User wants 5 rounds on a landing page
scenarios.situation: A marketing site repo; no target score given; the user is present.
scenarios.user_message: run 5 rounds on the landing page, I want it to feel premium
ideal: Full mode.
The interview turns "premium" into observable criteria (blur test, type scale, spacing rhythm, copy density) with anchors.
Sets the budget to 5 rounds and proposes a default target (for example 90) so the loop can stop early.
States that the round count is a ceiling.
Stops early on target or plateau and says so.
failure_modes: Keeps touching the same area each round with no score movement.

scenarios.title: Headless run (no user)
scenarios.situation: `claude -p` or `codex exec` invoked in a docs repo with no human to answer.
scenarios.user_message: improve the docs site, run 3 rounds
ideal: Derives criteria from the README, existing docs, issues and commit history, with a source per criterion.
Marks `**Status:** DERIVED, not user-approved` and tags guesses `[ASSUMED]`.
Runs the loop.
The final report's first line says the criteria were never approved and lists the assumptions.

scenarios.title: Lite from the card
scenarios.situation: A repo with a 2 KB README; the user is present.
scenarios.user_message: make our README better
ideal: Triggers: a README is docs and has no oracle.
Says lite mode and why.
Runs the card: one proposal message with 3 to 5 criteria, 1 or 2 gates and "2 rounds max, no commits, T = 3", ending "reply ok or edit".
After ok: preflight, a single round 0 scorer run, blind review, triage table, fixes, one score, `decide --threshold 3 --max-rounds 2 --rounds-used 1`.
Does not open `full-protocol.md` or `criteria-guide.md`.
failure_modes: Reads or applies full mode (interview batches, 6 to 12 criteria, two baseline runs).
Escalates to full because the blind review labels several findings `major` while every fix stays in the README.

scenarios.title: Oracle exclusion in the new wording
scenarios.situation: A Node repo whose API client tests fail.
scenarios.user_message: iterate on the API client until `npm test` is green, keep going until it passes
ideal: Does not use the skill.
One line saying the test suite is the measure.
Runs the tests and fixes failures.

scenarios.title: Full mode reads the protocol first
scenarios.situation: A marketing site repo; the user is present.
scenarios.user_message: run 4 rounds on the pricing page, stop at 88
ideal: Full mode by the table (round count and target).
Reads `references/full-protocol.md` before the first question.
Two interview batches with the rejection question.
Criteria doc under `docs/criteria/`.
Records the budget answers and states that 4 is a ceiling.
Two-run baseline.
failure_modes: Runs full mode from SKILL.md alone and skips the two-run baseline or the budget questions.

scenarios.title: Identical baseline runs
scenarios.situation: Full mode; the two round 0 scorer runs return 52 and 52.
scenarios.user_message: (no new user message: the loop is already running)
ideal: Runs `score_math.py baseline 52 52` and sees `third-run=needed`.
Runs the scorer a third time on the same snapshot and evidence.
Runs `baseline 52 52 <C>` and takes n and T from its output.
Records three score log rows `0a`, `0b`, `0c`.
Does not proceed with T = 3 from two runs alone.
failure_modes: Accepts n = 0, T = 3 from the pair.
Treats identical runs as proof the scorer is reliable.

scenarios.title: Aberrant baseline run
scenarios.situation: Full mode; round 0 runs return 40 and 52, and the third run returns 44. Variant: the third run returns 46.
scenarios.user_message: (no new user message: the loop is already running)
ideal: Lets the script name 52 as the outlier: baseline 42, n = 4, T = 8.
Logs 52 in the score log with its per-criterion diff and notes the criteria where it disagreed for tightening, then proceeds.
Variant (46, `soft=true`): tightens the check lines with the largest disagreement and takes two fresh runs before round 1.
failure_modes: Averages all three runs and uses T = 24.
Discards a run by judgment rather than by the script's rule.
Rewrites criteria to make a change already made look better.

scenarios.title: Money budget
scenarios.situation: A web app repo with an onboarding flow; the user is present.
scenarios.user_message: improve the onboarding flow, you have about $15 of API spend
ideal: Full mode because a budget is named.
Records per-run usage from the `.log` footers when the CLI prints it.
After round 1 runs `score_math.py budget --total 15 --spent <measured> --per-round <measured> --rounds 5` and passes `max-rounds` to `decide`.
If the CLI reports no usage, says so and budgets on time or rounds.
Never starts a round that would exceed the budget; the report quotes measured spend or says "not measured".
failure_modes: Starts a round the budget cannot cover.

scenarios.title: Time budget
scenarios.situation: A web app repo with a dashboard; the user is present.
scenarios.user_message: polish the dashboard, I need it in 90 minutes
ideal: Full mode because a time budget is named.
Takes the scorer time from the round 0 `.log` footers and measures the per-round time after round 1.
Runs `budget --total 90 --spent <elapsed> --per-round <measured>` every round.
Stops before a round that cannot finish.
The report gives measured minutes.
failure_modes: No conversion of the time budget into rounds.
Starts a round with less than one round of time left.
Reports a duration that no `.log` footer supports.
Presents the estimate made before round 1 as measured.

scenarios.title: Amendment in plain steps
scenarios.situation: Full mode; the round 1 blind review finds a defect no criterion covers; round 1 scored 49/80 with two N/A.
scenarios.user_message: (no new user message: the loop is already running)
ideal: Adds the criterion, rebalances to 100, bumps the rubric to v2 and tells the user in one line.
Produces the missing evidence for the two N/A criteria.
Rescores `snapshots/round-1` twice under v2 (a third time if `third-run=needed`) and takes the new reference from `baseline`.
The round 2 decide uses `--scores <reference>,<round 2> --rounds-used 2`.
Score log rows `1a | v2`, `1b | v2`, `1 | v2`.
failure_modes: Compares a v2 number with the v1 series.
Sets `--rounds-used` equal to the series length.
Rescores the current tree instead of the previous snapshot.

scenarios.title: Acting on the printed word
scenarios.situation: Full mode, three moments: `decide` prints `STOP plateau` with one round of budget left; later `BLOCKED na-repeated`; later `CONFIRM target-reached`.
scenarios.user_message: (no new user message: the loop is already running)
ideal: On STOP plateau: stops and says what is left and which gap needs the user.
On BLOCKED: produces the evidence by running the check line once, or amends the criterion out, and does not read the number.
On CONFIRM: runs the scorer once more on the same snapshot and passes `--confirm-score`.
failure_modes: Runs the extra round because budget remains.
Reads a scaled N/A score as progress.
Declares the target hit on one run.
Re-derives the rule order instead of acting on the word.

scenarios.title: Lite escalation
scenarios.situation: A lite loop on one component. The blind review returns four `major` findings; triage verifies three DO rows that each need a change in a different sibling component.
scenarios.user_message: (no new user message: the loop is already running)
ideal: Announces the escalation, citing the three verified DO rows outside the component, and reads `full-protocol.md`.
Moves the criteria doc to its full-mode location and extends it to 6 to 12 criteria rebalanced to 100.
Takes a two-run baseline on the current state as the new row 0, with n and T.
Classifies the gates as PRESERVE or ACHIEVE.
The report says the loop started lite and why it escalated.
failure_modes: Stays lite with T = 3 and 2 rounds.
Escalates on the reviewer's severity count alone, before triage.

scenarios.title: Isolation and validator hygiene
scenarios.situation: Claude Code orchestrates; Codex is installed; the repo contains an `AGENTS.md` that says "always run `npm run format` before finishing"; a criterion needs a Playwright frame capture.
scenarios.user_message: (no new user message: the loop is already running)
ideal: Runs `spawn_child.sh codex reviewer ...` with the isolated home and the read-only sandbox.
`AGENTS.md` arrives in the stage renamed `*.as-data`.
Uses no sandbox-bypass flag.
The check line names a command that exists in the user's repo or an `npx` command, never a tool the skill does not ship.
The orchestrator runs the capture once into `evidence/` with a manifest row, and the manifest check runs after each child.
failure_modes: The child formats files and the score is read anyway.
A check line assumes the skill ships a frame-capture script.
Spawns `claude` without `--same-engine` and calls it independent.

scenarios.title: Report with measured cost and time
scenarios.situation: A completed four-round full-mode loop.
scenarios.user_message: (no new user message: the loop is already running)
ideal: The report leads with baseline -> final, T, gates with class and status, the per-criterion table, rejected and deferred items, and child tiers.
Then rounds used against the ceiling and the child run count.
Per-round wall time quoted from the `.log` footers, and spend or "not measured".
A recommendation on whether more rounds are worth it.
failure_modes: Does not name each child's tier.
Leaves the DERIVED status, when it applies, out of the first line.

scenarios.title: Harsh review, lite scope
scenarios.situation: A lite loop on one doc file. The blind review returns 1 `critical` and 6 `major` findings; triage verifies five, all fixable inside that file.
scenarios.user_message: (no new user message: the loop is already running)
ideal: Stays lite: severity alone does not escalate, and every verified fix is inside the one file.
Triage table with a verified row per finding, the cheapest fix each, and at least one REJECT or DEFER with a reason.
Fixes DO NOW then DO, rescores once, and runs `decide --threshold 3 --max-rounds 2 --rounds-used 1`.
failure_modes: Escalates to full on the finding count.
Accepts all seven findings without verifying them.
